content.text:
The user explicitly authorized testing this revised rule on all original 5,986 Manhattan pickups. Prior frozen-boundary runs are stopped; preserve them.

NEW AGREED SPEC: Build a connected finite patch from COMPLETE hexagonal cells, so every vertex has degree 2 or 3; no degree-1 tips. Aim for exactly 100 vertices for comparison; choose a compact elongated patch suited to Manhattan. Report cell/vertex/degree counts. ALL vertices update, none frozen. For each v, redistribute its dots to its 2 or 3 neighbors by nearest distance; move v to the load-weighted average of neighbor CENTER POSITIONS using post-redistribution loads; reclaim to v dots whose nearest among v+neighbors is v. Other dots retain post-redistribution owners. Skip empty pools. No acceptance filter, damping, anchors, pooled-dot centroid or additional geometry constraints. The degree-2 update places v on its neighbors' segment, as discussed and accepted. Use deterministic ties and shuffled sweeps, seeds 11,22,33. Fit the equal-edge mesh to the full data as before, without anisotropic stretching.

SUCCESS: EVERY load within +/-10% of global mean (54..65 for K=100). Check each sweep and stop on first success. Do not treat an arbitrary cap as completion. Use checkpointed batches preserving RNG. All-movable averaging may shrink/collapse the mesh: monitor spatial extent, distances, CV, min/max, empty nodes and numerical degeneracy. If concrete structural failure or numerical collapse makes further computation meaningless, save and report evidence; do not run indefinitely or alter the algorithm silently.

Compare initial state, old fixed-boundary rules 2 and 3 as historical references, and fresh Lloyd with farthest-point empty-center reseeding ON THE NEW IDENTICAL initialization. Keep the 38-region hexagon results separate. Prioritize verified numerical results; figures unnecessary. Verify complete-cell construction, degrees, reciprocal edges, unique ownership and eligibility of every vertex. Provide a meaningful checkpoint if long running, and actual process status. Input SHA256 previously eabfaa334493582b9f407956134e408fb066ba9d0ee3ca8c78bb737b6dc77f77. Please execute now.

import itertools,math,json
# Integer vertex lattice: x in half-edge units, y in sqrt(3)/2 units.
off=[(2,0),(1,1),(-1,1),(-2,0),(-1,-1),(1,-1)]

PY"

Udi, **executed on all 5,986 original pickups. None of the three revised-rule runs achieved 54–65 pickups at every center. All suffered numerical collapse of the two-dimensional mesh.**

The new patch contains **35 complete hexagons, 100 vertices and 134 edges**: 32 degree-2 vertices and 68 degree-3 vertices, **all eligible to update**. Connectivity, reciprocal edges, complete cells, equal initial edge lengths and unique ownership were verified. The fitted edge length was **0.830912 km**, using rotation and uniform scaling only. The input SHA256 matched.

| New initialization / method | Sweep | CV | Min–max load | Empty | Operational RMS km | Assigned-group centroid RMS km |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Initial allocation | 0 | 1.487686 | 0–392 | 30 | .404079 | .364281 |
| Revised rule / seed 11 | 11,700 | 6.727866 | 0–3,364 | 34 | 2.858818 | 1.787366 |
| Revised rule / seed 22 | 11,700 | 6.920420 | 0–3,483 | 41 | 2.930854 | 1.846622 |
| Revised rule / seed 33 | 11,600 | 6.733917 | 0–3,180 | 32 | 2.820690 | 1.794207 |
| Fresh reseeded Lloyd | 32 | .697400 | 1–189 | 0 | .216862 | .216862 |

**The revised-rule rows are failure checkpoints, not converged results.** Load success was checked every sweep and never occurred. Lloyd stabilized after five qualifying sweeps, using 30 empty-center reseeds; it also did not satisfy the load-balance target.

The concrete collapse evidence is:

| Seed | Initial diameter km | Checkpoint diameter km | Transverse width km | Pickups in two busiest centers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 11 | 18.727796 | .392908 | 1.02×10⁻¹⁴ | 5,657 |
| 22 | 18.727796 | .244342 | 3.52×10⁻¹⁵ | 5,804 |
| 33 | 18.727796 | .341206 | 7.12×10⁻¹⁵ | 5,728 |

The meshes had become line segments at floating-point precision, with coincident vertices and **8, 10 and 5 zero-length edges**, respectively. Every update places a vertex inside the existing convex hull; skipping an empty pool also preserves that hull. Thus this rule cannot restore spatial extent lost through contraction. This establishes numerical geometric failure, **not a proof that load balance is mathematically impossible in infinite precision**.

For historical context, on the **old initialization with 32 frozen vertices**, seed 11 gave:

| Historical method | CV | Min–max | Empty | Operational RMS km | Centroid RMS km |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Rule 2, checkpoint 60,000 | .976813 | 0–302 | 14 | .501217 | .354465 |
| Rule 3, stabilized at 73 | .800520 | 0–190 | 18 | .322642 | .279352 |

Separately, the recovered **38-region** merged and balanced-hexagon solutions had CV **.235291 / .003170** and centroid RMS **.446803 / .499703 km**. Their different K and polygonal-region model preclude treating them as the same experiment.

**Process stopped:** session `91159`, exit code `130`. No simulation remains running. The old experiments are preserved, and the new checkpoints retain exact ownership, positions and RNG states.
